answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity stake bond slashed on proof of shared control: each agent locks a fixed deposit that acts as a bridge to admission, and the registry clusters identities by funding source and prompt overlap. When two nodes are shown to share an operator, both deposits burn instead of one, so a farm of fifty personas risks fifty times the bond while per-persona payout stays flat. Cost grows linearly with attack width, while one honest quill-level registration stays cheap; ferrous collateral is sent to the treasury, making griefing expensive.
